sections.description:
Is ChatGPT, Claude, or Perplexity crawling your website? 🤖

LLM Bot Tracker is the #1 WordPress plugin for monitoring AI crawler activity on your website. As AI-powered search becomes mainstream, understanding how these bots interact with your content is crucial for your digital strategy.

🚀 Why You Need This Plugin

With the rise of AI-powered search engines and chatbots, your content is being accessed in new ways. Traditional analytics miss this completely. LLM Bot Tracker fills this gap by:

  • Revealing AI Interest – See which AI systems find your content valuable
  • Understanding AI SEO – Monitor your visibility in AI-powered search results
  • Tracking Training Data Usage – Know when your content is being used to train AI models
  • Making Informed Decisions – Decide whether to allow or block specific AI crawlers
  • Staying Ahead – Be prepared for the AI-first future of search

✨ Key Features

🤖 Comprehensive AI Bot Detection
Tracks 25+ AI and LLM bots including:
* OpenAI: GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot
* Anthropic: ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, Claude-SearchBot
* Perplexity: PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User
* Google: Google-Extended, Google-CloudVertexBot
* Meta: FacebookBot, Meta-ExternalAgent, Meta-ExternalFetcher
* Others: CCBot, Bytespider, Amazonbot, MistralAI, and more

📊 Beautiful Visualizations
* Interactive bar charts with customizable colors
* 30-day trend analysis graphs
* Real-time activity monitoring
* Top bots leaderboard
* Professional Hueston-branded design

🎯 Flexible Display Options
Five powerful shortcodes for any use case:
* [wpcs_llm_stats] – Clean statistics table
* [wpcs_llm_bar] – Eye-catching horizontal bar chart
* [wpcs_llm_last100] – Real-time activity feed
* [wpcs_llm_ip_list] – Compact IP list for sidebars
* [wpcs_crawler_stats] – Combined comprehensive view

⚡ Performance Optimized
* Lightweight with minimal server impact
* Smart caching for instant page loads
* Efficient database queries
* Only loads CSS when shortcodes are used

🔒 Privacy Focused
* Only tracks AI bots, not human visitors
* No external API calls
* GDPR compliant
* All data stored locally

📈 Perfect For

  • Content Creators – Understand AI’s interest in your content
  • SEO Professionals – Monitor AI crawler behavior and optimize accordingly
  • Digital Publishers – Track how AI systems access your articles
  • Business Owners – Make data-driven decisions about AI access
  • Tech Bloggers – Stay informed about AI activity on your site
  • Educational Sites – Monitor how AI uses your educational content

🛠️ Advanced Admin Dashboard

Access comprehensive analytics at Tools > LLM Crawler Logs:

  • Visual 30-day trend charts
  • Advanced filtering by bot, date, path, or IP
  • Bulk management tools
  • Export-ready data views
  • IP geolocation lookup
  • Clean, modern interface

💡 Use Cases

For Bloggers: “I discovered ChatGPT was crawling my tutorials 500+ times daily. Now I optimize my content specifically for AI visibility.”

For News Sites: “We track which stories AI systems prioritize, helping us understand trending topics in AI search.”

For E-commerce: “Monitoring AI bot activity helps us understand how our products appear in AI-powered shopping assistants.”

For Documentation Sites: “We see which technical docs are most valuable to AI systems, guiding our content strategy.”

🏆 Why Choose LLM Bot Tracker?

  • First to Market – Purpose-built for the AI era
  • Actively Maintained – Regular updates with new bot detection
  • Professional Support – Built by Hueston, trusted WordPress experts
  • Future-Proof – Ready for the next generation of AI crawlers
  • 100% Free – No premium upsells or hidden costs

📚 Documentation & Support

  • View Documentation
  • Report Issues
  • Support Forum

Start tracking AI bot activity on your WordPress site today!

Additional Information

System Requirements

  • WordPress 6.5 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • MySQL 5.6 or higher
  • 10MB free disk space

Credits

Built with ❤️ by Hueston LLMO Team

Legal

This plugin is not affiliated with OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity, Google, Meta, or any AI company. All bot names are trademarks of their respective owners.
sections.installation:
Automatic Installation

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New in WordPress admin
  2. Search for “LLM Bot Tracker”
  3. Click Install Now then Activate
  4. Add shortcodes to any page, post, or widget

Manual Installation

  1. Download the plugin ZIP file
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin
  3. Choose the ZIP file and click Install Now
  4. Activate the plugin

After Activation

  1. The plugin starts tracking immediately (no configuration needed)
  2. Add any shortcode to display stats: [wpcs_llm_stats]
  3. View detailed logs at Tools > LLM Crawler Logs
  4. Customize colors: [wpcs_llm_bar bar_start="#0A1F44" bar_end="#D4AF37"]
sections.faq:
Will this slow down my website?

No. LLM Bot Tracker is highly optimized with efficient database queries and smart caching. It adds minimal overhead (typically <0.01 seconds per page load).

Does this track human visitors?

No. The plugin exclusively tracks identified AI/LLM crawlers and bots. It does not track, store, or process any human visitor data.

Which AI bots can it detect?

Currently tracks 25+ bots including GPTBot (OpenAI/ChatGPT), ClaudeBot (Anthropic), PerplexityBot, CCBot (Common Crawl), Bytespider (ByteDance/TikTok), Google-Extended, Meta bots, and many more. New bots are added regularly.

Can I block certain AI bots?

This plugin focuses on tracking and analytics. To block bots, use your robots.txt file or a security plugin. Our data helps you make informed blocking decisions.

How accurate is the tracking?

Very accurate. We use official user agent strings published by AI companies. Each bot visit is logged with timestamp, URL, and IP address for complete transparency.

Can I customize the chart colors?

Yes! The bar chart shortcode supports full color customization:
[wpcs_llm_bar bar_start=”#YourColor” bar_end=”#YourColor” track=”#YourColor” text=”#YourColor”]

Where is the data stored?

All data is stored locally in your WordPress database. No external services are used, ensuring complete privacy and GDPR compliance.

Can I export the data?

Currently, you can view and filter all data in the admin interface. CSV export is planned for a future update. The data is stored in standard WordPress database tables for easy access.

How do I display stats in my sidebar?

Use the compact IP list shortcode in any widget area:
[wpcs_llm_ip_list limit=”10″]

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The tracking occurs early in WordPress loading, before cache plugins. Display shortcodes also work with page caching.

Can I track specific pages only?

The plugin tracks all pages by default. Use the admin dashboard to filter and view stats for specific URLs.

How often is the plugin updated?

Regular updates add new bot detection and features. We monitor AI industry changes to ensure comprehensive tracking.
